environment.description: Same Flask application deployed in namespace 'asset-search-prod' on a k8s 1.28 cluster with Pod Security Standards enforced at 'restricted' level via namespace label (pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted). The pod spec includes securityContext with runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, and drops ALL capabilities. The container runs with seccomp profile RuntimeDefault. Additionally, a Cilium L7 NetworkPolicy is applied that performs HTTP-layer inspection on ingress traffic to the pod, with a rule that denies any request where the query string or path contains characters matching the pattern [<>"'();] (configured via CiliumNetworkPolicy with HTTP header match rules using regex on the :path pseudo-header). The Cilium policy spec uses a 'rules.http' section with method GET and a headerFilter that rejects requests where the URL-decoded :path matches the dangerous character set. This effectively blocks reflected XSS payloads from reaching the application layer since the attack requires injecting HTML/JS via the 'q' parameter.
